stories.title: Ultrasound overlay records high false-positive rate
stories.summary: A preliminary clinical evaluation of an obstetric ultrasound colour overlay identified two high-risk placentas in a cohort of 55 pregnancies. The tool also generated 18 false-positive classifications where normal placentas were incorrectly labelled as low-lying. The technology aims to support screening in settings with shortages of trained sonographers.

stories.title: Colorectal cancer video reliability varies by platform
stories.summary: A study of 300 videos across YouTube, Douyin, and Bilibili found significant differences in the reliability and quality of colorectal cancer information. Researchers noted that these disparities were partly explained by uploader composition and video duration. Social media networks have become primary hubs for individuals seeking medical guidance.

stories.title: Study links product design to hypertension in Nigeria
stories.summary: Product design attributes are significantly associated with increased odds of hypertension among adults in Ibadan, Nigeria, according to a study in BMC Public Health. Researchers identified design features as the only commercial determinant domain linked to elevated blood pressure. Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of death locally.

stories.title: Pact designs kaleidoscopic identity for Anagram
stories.summary: Pact has created a brand identity for venture firm Anagram based on a single square that rearranges into various glyphs and grids. The firm seeks to bring the ownership economy to the masses. Pact describes the resulting personality as pioneering, based, optimistic, and fun. It never settles.

stories.summary: Brazil state lender Caixa Econômica Federal has updated its branding for the first time in 29 years. Agency Tátil led the work, incorporating a savings box and roof motif into the bank's existing X. The previous identity was described as having begun to look drab and dated.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings for video calls
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings, a feature that puts its AI into video calls as a participant. The tool can answer questions, log notes, and generate whiteboards during sessions. It is currently in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, with Google Meet as the only supported platform.

stories.title: Adobe allows third-party AI agents to edit native files
stories.summary: Adobe announced at its MAX 2026 conference that third-party AI agents, including Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini, will be authorized to edit native Photoshop, Premiere, and Illustrator files directly. The company argues that agentic AI has moved from the margins of professional creative work into its center.

stories.title: Adobe introduces Brand Intelligence for content governance
stories.summary: Adobe is promoting Brand Intelligence to help organizations manage brand consistency across content. The company says the system uses artificial intelligence to evaluate branded content by combining visual analysis and contextual reasoning. It aims to assist teams struggling to maintain standards as their content spreads across various channels.

stories.title: Adobe expands AI across Creative Cloud and opens to chatbots
stories.summary: Adobe has expanded AI features across its Creative Cloud suite and released a Model Context Protocol to let chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude use Adobe tools. The company is also moving into prototyping with its new Builder tool, while its AI agent becomes proactive to gather user context.

stories.title: Adobe brings AI agents to Premiere and After Effects
stories.summary: Adobe has introduced Creative Agent to power AI assistants across its video and design applications. The updates allow creators to hand off complex, multi-step tasks to an assistant while retaining final approval. The company says this lets artists delegate work while keeping the final say on the result.

stories.title: Adobe and Disney form multi-year AI partnership
stories.summary: Disney has signed a strategic alliance with Adobe, naming the software maker an Official AI Innovation Partner. The deal provides Disney creative teams with early access to Adobe tools and custom Firefly Foundry models trained on Disney character attributes, environments, and visual styles for use in production.

stories.title: Ecopilot project uses AI for sustainable design
stories.summary: The Horizon Europe project Ecopilot combines artificial intelligence and sustainability assessment to help companies make environmental decisions during product design. Aimplas is contributing by developing CO2-based coatings and generating environmental data. The initiative brings together 14 organizations to develop digital tools for safer and more sustainable furniture.

stories.summary: Canva has launched Affinity for iPad, combining sketching, vector design, and photo editing into a single tablet application. Core tools are free, while AI features require a premium account. The company says the app answers demand from existing users following the integration of Affinity on desktop.

stories.summary: Adobe unveiled 10 experimental technologies during its MAX Sneaks session, focusing on AI-based image, video, and audio editing. Features included a tool for painting along curved surfaces and automation for detecting user intent. stories.summary: KT has launched KDS 2.0, a design system that uses AI to automate app layouts and customer notification messages. The company claims this will improve development efficiency and standardize service interfaces. The AI agent is now responsible for drafting and reviewing communications that were previously handled by humans.

stories.title: IED Torino wins Maruti Suzuki DesignXathon
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki concluded its second DesignXathon, where over 450 students competed to envision vehicles for 2036. Italy’s IED Torino took the top prize after presenting a 1:8-scale prototype at the company’s Gurugram studio. Two teams from NID Gandhinagar secured the second and third positions.

stories.summary: Ahmedabad-based iMAC Design and Engineering Services received a Gold award at the 16th CII Design Excellence Awards. stories.summary: Five months after launching, Bangalore-based Burgundy Studio has won two National Gold awards at the 12th afaqs! Foxglove Awards. The studio was recognized for its own website and its work on a corporate site for EliteEPM. The firm focuses on web design and development.

stories.summary: Built99 has launched an annual list of 99 studios to connect Indian architecture with the global market. Backed by designboom and ArchDaily, the initiative promotes low-impact construction and regional craft. It aims to spotlight practices defined by cultural responsiveness and the use of native materials.

stories.title: Grohe hosts bathroom design forum in India
stories.summary: Grohe hosted its inaugural Circle Intellect Forum in New Delhi, bringing together 19 architects to discuss the future of Indian bathrooms. The closed-door session focused on evolving consumer expectations and industry solutions. The participants examined what Indian bathrooms require today to meet modern demands.

stories.summary: Clawlab has raised over $15 million in a Pre-A3 funding round led by miHoYo. The startup develops smart tools for textile creation and has now secured approximately $25 million in total funding. The company says AI software is currently commanding much of the market.

stories.title: QB MEN raises pre-seed funding for printed menswear
stories.summary: Jaipur-based D2C brand QB MEN has raised pre-seed funding led by BeyondSeed. The company plans to use the capital for brand building and distribution. Unlike conventional inventory-led fashion brands, the company follows a demand-led production approach. It offers shirts, kurtas, and jackets featuring traditional Indian prints.

stories.title: Biomatter raises €16.2 million for custom enzymes
stories.summary: Vilnius-based Biomatter has raised €16.2 million to develop AI-designed custom enzymes. The company aims to create proteins that are not found in nature. The full details of the funding and the company's specific technical roadmap are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Product designers split on AI integration
stories.summary: Product design teams are divided on how to implement AI, according to discussions at the PUSH UX conference in Munich. Some teams are cautiously experimenting with the technology, while others have integrated it into daily workflows. The difference reflects how teams organize their work and understand their processes.

stories.title: John Massey, Chicago modernist, dies at 95
stories.summary: Chicago modernist graphic designer John Massey died this past September at age 95. His work was recorded and collected by peers and institutions. Scholars often worry about benign neglect regarding significant figures in design history. Obscurity is an awful fate.

stories.title: Portfolio Night names 2026 all-stars
stories.summary: The One Club for Creativity has named its Portfolio Night All-Stars, a group of young creatives selected by industry professionals from city hosts worldwide. Established in 2003, the program is described as the world's largest advertising portfolio review. It aims to help the next generation of talent.

stories.title: Three Indian creatives named ADC Young Guns finalists
stories.summary: Three creative professionals from India have been named finalists in the 24th edition of the ADC Young Guns competition. The program recognizes emerging talent aged 30 or younger. The finalists are among 94 selected from 20 countries, evaluated by a jury of more than 100 professionals.

stories.title: Tanmay Saxena on surreal photography
stories.summary: London-based artist Tanmay Saxena has transitioned from a banking career to surreal photography. His work draws on personal memories and the unexpected moments he encounters while wandering. He recently created a series titled Superhero Downtime during a period when his own creative powers were not firing.

stories.title: Springetts marks 50 years in business
stories.summary: Brand agency Springetts is celebrating its 50th anniversary. The firm, which has named products including The Happy Egg Co. and Frubes, describes itself as a brand life-stage agency. It has operated through recessions and retail revolutions. Most UK businesses do not make it to their fifth birthday.

stories.title: Canva restructures 22 percent of global workforce
stories.summary: Canva is restructuring 22 percent of its global workforce, affecting 1,271 employees. CEO Melanie Perkins described the decision as the hardest moment in the company's thirteen-year history. Business experts have praised the communication of the decision, even as the company acknowledges the serious consequences for those affected.

stories.title: Canva offers exit packages following layoffs
stories.summary: Canva is cutting 1,271 jobs, or 22 percent of its global staff, citing slowed growth. The company is offering an exit package that includes salary support, healthcare, career assistance, MacBooks, and startup grants. The CEO shared the news in a message published on the company website.

stories.title: Canva details support package for departing staff
stories.summary: Canva is cutting 1,271 jobs, roughly 22 percent of its global workforce, as it prepares for an internal overhaul. The company has offered a support package to those leaving, including LinkedIn Premium subscriptions and MacBooks. The cuts will affect teams across all 37 countries where Canva operates.

research.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
research.summary: Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
